notes: All records built from pages fetched on 2026-11-02. The shared WebSearch budget ran out mid-task, so bodies not found before that point (see next notes) were left out rather than guessed.

Federal: EO 14031 (the order that re-established the White House Initiative on AANHPI and the President's Advisory Commission) is listed among the orders rescinded by EO 14148 (Federal Register 2025-01-28). whitehouse.gov/aanhpi returned HTTP 404 on 2026-11-02. No successor body was found in the sources fetched; no 2026 reinstatement was found.

Not confirmed (no fetched source, so omitted): state AAPI commissions in Texas, Colorado, Georgia and Nevada; AAPI bodies of the cities of Los Angeles, New York, Seattle, San Francisco and Honolulu; a Washington State legislative AAPI caucus; AAPI-specific offices at HHS, Education, Labor and USDA. Only Interior's Office of Native Hawaiian Relations was confirmed at federal agency level.

Status wording: 'active' means a fetched page dated or live in 2025-2026 shows the body operating. 'unclear' means the body exists in fetched sources but the latest evidence is older or undated (dates given in x). Several legislative caucuses are 'unclear' for that reason, not because they are known to have ended.

Pages that blocked automated fetching (HTTP 403 or bot check): dos.ny.gov, mass.gov, mn.gov/capm, oha.org (OHA facts came from a separate fetch of the OHA about page), capitol.hawaii.gov, ilga.gov (TLS error). Their URLs are listed as official URLs but were not opened directly.

NCAPA: the member page's meta description says 41 members but the page body lists 45 (45 recorded). The page shows no organization website links (only a LEAD Filipino link and a malformed aapidata.com link), so each URL was checked by fetching the organization's own site and matching its name. Nine members have u '' and unverified true because their sites could not be fetched or matched.

Excluded on purpose: appealforcommunities.org and njamf.com. Both domains returned unrelated commercial content (gambling and jewelry text) when fetched, so they are not listed as APPEAL's or NJAMF's websites. Verify the current domains by hand.

Advancing Justice: AAJC's affiliation page (fetched) says the affiliation has four members: AAJC (Washington, DC), Atlanta, Chicago and Southern California. Asian Law Caucus is not listed there, and advancingjustice-alc.org now redirects to asianlawcaucus.org. ALC is therefore not recorded as a current member.

Stop AAPI Hate: its Who We Are page names three founders (AAPI Equity Alliance, Chinese for Affirmative Action, the Asian American Studies Department at San Francisco State University), founded March 19, 2020. The brief's 'Asian Pacific Policy and Planning Council' does not appear on that page. The SF State department's website could not be fetched, so its URL is blank.

Asian American Federation: its member page shows 35 member agencies and 22 partner agencies only as logo links, with no names in the page text. Member names were taken from each organization's own site title. Six members whose sites could not be fetched carry unverified true. Partner agencies are not recorded here.

Maryland's Governor's Commission on South-Asian American Affairs (EO 01.01.2025.04) is included because the Maryland Manual lists it beside the Asian-Pacific American commission. The Maryland Manual text for the APA commission was cut off in the fetched copy before the 2025 changes; check it against the current manual.
Territories: Guam, CNMI and American Samoa entries are existence-only (status unclear). Each is a government office for indigenous or Pacific Islander affairs, not a general AAPI commission.
